coverage_notes: Frozen vs. audited candidate: the round4 candidate has the same 31 blocks as round3, in the same order, with the same scan, key, language, kind and text values. I compared them by reading both side by side, not with a byte diff, because no shell was available. The only difference is that round4 drops the top-level 'scope' string from round3 ('Source blocks are keyed inventory, not a statement of recitation order...'). That string is metadata, not source text, so it does not affect fidelity. Whoever owns encoding or ordering may want to put it back.

Ruling 310a (question-310-v1.png, top crop; s224 gevurot_open, line 5): the candidate reads 'וּמִי דּוֹמֶה לָּךְ מֶלֶךְ', with a dagesh in the lamed of לָּךְ. This matches a_lamed_dagesh=true. The other lamed in the crop, in מֶלֶךְ, has no dagesh in the candidate, which matches other_displayed_lameds_dagesh=false.

Ruling 310b (bottom crop; s224 tifen): the candidate reads 'חָלִילָה לְּךָ אֱלֹהֵי', with a dagesh in the lamed of לְּךָ. This matches b_lamed_dagesh=true. The other displayed lameds are both lameds of חָלִילָה and the lamed of אֱלֹהֵי. None has a dagesh in the candidate, which matches other_displayed_lameds_dagesh=false.

In both the crop and the full s224 page, the dot inside each questioned lamed is too small to confirm independently. I saw nothing incompatible with the human ruling, such as a clearly empty lamed counter, so I accepted 310 as final, as instructed.
Human311–316 concern other pages. I did not apply them to scans 224–227 and did not check them. 312 (ח׳) and 314 (the Shabbat rubric) do not affect any block here.

Page coverage, unchanged consonants, vowels, rubrics, speaker cues and English readings for s224–s227 rely on the complete round3 image audit. It reported no findings, and the text it audited is unchanged. I looked at the s224 full page again only to place the two 310 words in context. This approval covers source fidelity only. It does not approve encoding, the registry, generated recitation order, or exports.
